speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy having trouble feeding and your tummy looks swollen. Can you tell me how long this has been happening and if you have been vomiting?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: That abdominal tenderness is concerning. Has he passed any stool or gas recently, and have you noticed any "currant jelly" stools or a palpable abdominal mass?

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text: No fever or vomiting is good, but the worsening pain on palpation and lack of gas/stool are worrisome. Has he passed *any* stool or gas in the last 24 hours? REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_X-Ray

speaker: Patient
text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Intussusception (likely ileocolic) pending confirmation of an air-contrast enema or abdominal ultrasound showing the "target sign."
